ideas.title: The 10-Second Balance Glitch
ideas.angle: An interactive test that forces the viewer to stand up and try a physical impossibility. It highlights the science of center of gravity and neuromuscular feedback. It triggers comments from people trying to 'beat' the glitch and failing.
ideas.reason: Interactive physical challenges currently dominate Shorts (VVSA 85%+) because they force the viewer to stop scrolling and physically engage. This specific center-of-gravity trick is a classic viral 'glitch' that generates high engagement through failed attempts.
sources: Scientific American - The Physics of Balance
Biophysics of Human Posture and Center of Mass Research

ideas.title: The Troxler Effect Visual Hack
ideas.angle: A live optical illusion where the viewer stares at a cross on screen until the surrounding colors vanish. This demonstrates the 'Troxler Effect' where neurons ignore unchanging stimuli. High APV because the viewer must stare for 15+ seconds.
ideas.reason: Visual sensory adaptation tests have a massive 'stickiness' factor. Viewers stay until the end to see if it works, often rewatching (APV >100%) to ensure they didn't blink or miss the transition.

ideas.title: The Instant Calm Survival Reset
ideas.angle: Explains how splashing ice-cold water on your face triggers an ancient survival reflex that instantly drops your heart rate. It’s a 'life-hack' for anxiety/stress. It prompts users to comment their 'stress levels' or results.
ideas.reason: Practical, 'forbidden' knowledge style body hacks perform exceptionally well with 25-45 age demographics. It combines survival science with a 'secret' physical shortcut that provides immediate value.
sources: Frontiers in Physiology - The Mammalian Dive Response
